headline: Validation of nanopore long-read methods against controls and reference data
label: Long Read Benchmarking And Calibration
summary: Recent nanopore studies test modification and resistance calling against controls, GLORI references, and real-time QC workflows.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluation of nanopore-based calls against independent references or controls. The eLife framework benchmarks Dorado versions for direct-RNA m6A calling against GLORI, adds stringent filtering, and reports cell-specific m6A proportions at conserved sites. A preprint on Dorado's inosine model for A-to-I editing finds that ADAR-deficient controls and sufficient depth are essential for assessing detection. mRNAspect proposes real-time quality control for therapeutic mRNA from direct RNA reads, with N1-methylpseudouridine bias correction and poly(A) correction. NanoHIV-DR provides a Nextflow workflow for HIV-1 drug resistance profiling, offering both consensus-based and read-level variant detection. The more specific element is explicit control-based validation and calibration of modification-calling pipelines, with conclusions tied to the data type and application.
